messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: p99 latency spike detected for customer PolarBank (VPC: polarbank-eu-west, Dedicated pool: db-polar-eu1). Alerts started at 1965432096. Threshold breached: p99 > 1.5s for 5m.
jamie_oncall: I'm on it — grabbing logs and allocation. @ryan_eng want me to start GC/evictions on KV cache or prefer scaling first?
ryan_eng: hi - check GPU and rpc latency first. If rpc tail latency > 200ms across racks, scaling won't help. Pulling tail -> `redis latency: 12-18ms`, `rpc p99: 420ms` on the control-plane -> looks like RPC fanout is the hotspot.
chris_ops: Confirmed. `netstat` shows connection spikes on nodes polar-eu1-{03..06}. CPU fine, GPU util ~40-55%, qps per-host doubled. Likely burst from customer run.
eva_infra: telemetry shows increased queue depth at the ingress LB in eu-west-1. Autoscaler didn't kick due to pool lock (reserved capacity). We can temporarily increase pool size, but need account approval for burst > reserved.
amy_csm: @jamie_oncall I pinged PolarBank CSM on phone — they authorized emergency cross-region routing and temporary burst up to +3 nodes for 30m. They want minimal change and rollback after.
jamie_oncall: OK — plan: 1) add +3 to polarbank-eu-west reserved pool, 2) if RPC tail still >300ms after 90s, shift 20% of traffic to eu-west-3 warm pool (same region family) via routing rule, 3) evict heavy KV prefixes for the duration. Any objections? :thinking_face:
miguel_ops: No objections. I'll run scale now. Command: ```bash
redwoodctl pools scale --pool polarbank-eu-west --add-nodes 3 --reason "p99 emergency burst"
```
deploybot: Scaling request received. Provisioning 3 nodes to pool polarbank-eu-west. Expected ready in ~70s.
jamie_oncall: while we wait, let's evict KV prefixes for bursty customers. ryan, which prefixes?
ryan_eng: `user_ctx:*` and `session_cache:polarbank:*` are hot. Evicting `session_cache:polarbank:*` should reduce fanout serialization. Command: ```bash
kvctl evict --prefix "session_cache:polarbank:" --cluster polarbank-vpc
```
chris_ops: evict issued. Observability: tailing logs — rpc p99 dropped from 420ms -> 310ms after eviction. Good.
eva_infra: deploybot reports nodes ready and in pool. Routing update in 20s.
deploybot: Nodes added. Pool healthy: 3 new nodes joined.
jamie_oncall: Rebalancing traffic now: ```bash
routingctl update --route polarbank-route --split 80:eu-west-1,20:eu-west-3 --sticky true --reason "emergency split"
```
ryan_eng: After split p99 at eu-west-1 = 260ms, eu-west-3 = 210ms. Overall p99 ~230ms. Still above SLO (200ms p99).
amy_csm: PolarBank on call says they're seeing improvement but still noticed slow page loads for a subset of requests. They approve temporary cross-region fallback to us-east-1 if eu-west-3 degrades.
miguel_ops: Suggest we also enable short-circuit fallback for large-context requests to a smaller model variant to reduce KV and memory pressure: `model-route: gpt-32k -> gpt-8k-small` for requests >16k tokens. Need eng signoff.
ryan_eng: Agree. I'll push a safe model-variant rule with canary 5% for the next 10m. If error rate spikes, auto-roll back. Command: ```bash
modelctl route --customer polarbank --condition "request.tokens > 16000" --variant gpt-8k-small --canary 0.05 --duration 10m
```
jamie_oncall: Canary applied. Monitoring for edge-case regressions.
chris_ops: Observability: error rate stable, latency trend downward. p99 now ~190ms overall. Looks within SLO for the moment.
eva_infra: Note: logs show increased retry rate from downstream proxy caused by 502s in one node (polar-eu1-04) before scale. I recommend marking that node as suspect and cordoning it for deeper postmortem.
jamie_oncall: cordon issued: `k8s: cordon polar-eu1-04` and instructed infra to collect heap/profile.
ryan_eng: I pulled async traces — contention around RPC goroutine pools and a hot file descriptor leak in our connection multiplexer. Patch incoming to reduce max idle connections and restart connector process on cordoned node.
chris_ops: Patch rolled with restart on polar-eu1-04. Post-restart metrics look normal.
jamie_oncall: Summary for handoff: - Root cause: sudden high-fanout job from PolarBank causing RPC tail spikes + KV hot prefixes. - Immediate mitigations: KV evict, +3 reserved nodes, split 20% to eu-west-3, model canary to smaller variant for >16k token requests, cordoned one node and restarted connector. - Customer approval for cross-region and +3 burst obtained.
amy_csm: PolarBank asks for timeline and RCA when we have it. They want confirmation we won't enable cross-region failover without notice going forward.
jamie_oncall: noted. Will prepare RCA and change control proposal. Handing off to chris_ops for monitoring and custody. I'm leaving the channel but reachable. :wave:
chris_ops: Taking over monitoring. I'll keep an eye for p99 and errors for 2h. If p99 climbs >220ms or errors >0.5% we'll revert routing split and increase pool.
jamie_oncall: thanks — handing to @chris_ops. Oncall notes pinned.
sre-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident severity downgraded to Sev-2.
miguel_ops: quick FYI — flagged for postmortem: investigate connection multiplexer FD leak and autoscaler behavior with reserved pools.
ryan_eng: I'll own the postmortem and open a follow-up ticket with action items (connmux fix, autoscaler adjustment, better tenant-level KV sharding).
jamie_oncall: closing the active warroom — final note: customer-facing update queued by @amy_csm. Thanks team :clap:
amy_csm: Customer update sent: "We performed emergency mitigations and restored latency within SLO. Further steps and permanent fix timeline to follow." PolarBank replied :thumbsup:.
chris_ops: logging handoff timestamp 1965432500 in incident tracker. I'll close after 2h of stable metrics.
jamie_oncall: great. good job everyone."
